h2: Cargo tanks, ASME pressure tanks and API 653 storage tanks in Washington: who inspects which
html:
Cargo tanks, ASME pressure tanks and API 653 storage tanks in Washington: who inspects which

"Tank inspection" in Washington covers three different rule sets, and the searches that reach this page show all three: DOT certified tank repair, ASME tank inspection in Spokane and API 653 storage tanks at terminals. Each has its own legally responsible inspector. Atlantis supplies conventional NDT, meaning ultrasonic thickness, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant and visual testing, under that inspector's direction. Atlantis is not a cargo tank repair facility, not a commissioned boiler and pressure vessel inspector and not an API 653 inspector.

DOT cargo tanks: registered facilities and qualified inspectors

Tank trucks and trailers built to DOT specifications are tested on the schedule in 49 CFR 180.407: external and internal visual inspection, lining checks, pressure and leakage tests, and thickness testing. Unlined tanks carrying lading corrosive to the tank must be thickness tested at least every two years, with a device accurate to plus or minus 0.002 inch. Whoever performs or witnesses those tests must meet the qualifications in 49 CFR 180.409. Repairs go to a facility holding a National Board "R" Certificate of Authorization for ASME-stamped tanks, or to an ASME "U" or National Board "R" holder for non-ASME tanks, and every facility doing that work must be registered under 49 CFR Part 107, Subpart F. So "DOT certified tank repair" means a registered repair shop. Atlantis can examine a repair weld by MT or PT, or take UT thickness readings, when that facility's qualified inspector asks for the data; the facility certifies the tank.

"ASME tank inspection" in Spokane and across the state

An "ASME tank" is usually a pressure vessel built and stamped to ASME Section VIII, such as an air receiver or a process vessel. In Washington those fall under the Department of Labor and Industries boiler and pressure vessel program, and certificate inspections are made by L&I inspectors or by insurers' inspectors holding a Washington commission. When that inspector wants remaining wall on a shell or head, or a crack check at a nozzle weld, Atlantis can take UT readings and run MT or PT. See ultrasonic testing in Spokane and magnetic particle testing in Spokane.

Terminal and plant storage tanks under API 653

For oil terminals and refineries, Washington adds a state layer on top of federal spill rules. The Department of Ecology's facility rule, WAC 173-180-330, requires tanks at regulated oil-handling facilities to be maintained, repaired and inspected under API 653 unless Ecology approves an equivalent strategy, and to be inspected under the standard's seismic provisions; the results feed the facility's spill risk analysis. In the Puget Sound earthquake setting, good shell and foundation data matter more than usual. Conventional NDT supplies much of it:

  • UT shell thickness by course and at nozzle necks, for the API 653 inspector's minimum thickness and remaining life calculation
  • MT or PT on the shell-to-bottom weld, repair welds and new nozzle reinforcing pads
  • Vacuum box leak testing of floor and repair welds
  • Visual records of roof, seals, wind girders, anchor bolts and foundation

Floor plate coverage beyond spot UT readings needs a floor-scanning method that the API 653 inspector specifies.

How Seattle-area providers compare

Mistras lists two western Washington branches, in Kent and in Burlington near the Skagit County refineries, and its Kent page names API 653, 570 and 510 inspection among its services. Registered cargo tank shops handle DOT tests themselves. Independent API 653 inspectors and integrity firms sign tank reports and often subcontract the NDT. Ask any provider:

  • Who is the legally responsible inspector for this tank, and will that person accept this company's data?
  • Are UT readings recorded by course, plate and orientation so they can be repeated next interval?
  • Which written practice certifies the technicians, and which ASNT Level III approved the MT, PT and UT procedures?
  • When will the report be issued? Agree it before mobilization.
